dossier.public_summary: The dip changes from nothing in some sectors to deep in others and transit depths are all over the place, sometimes larger than 1%. The star also shows a strong brightness swing at the dip period. Together with an unusually long grazing shape, this is not a stable planet transit.

reasons.why: depth changes catastrophically between sectors, per tool sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with p_constant_all 1.1947075693399775e-121. That plus the TESS-SPOC p_constant 0.038716415028036494 (marginal) and QLP p_constant 2.590312925849682e-78 proves the dip is not astrophysically steady.
individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent (chi2 1166.5566714261577 dof 308) with outliers to 21533 ppm (8.0 sigma, 19281 ppm at 6.7 sigma, etc), not a planet.

large out-of-transit swing ratio_to_depth 0.2431 chi2 49.23 dof 9 and fit density mismatch fit_log_density_ratio -1.834 star_density_penalty 95.83 favour a stellar/spotted/variable binary over a quiet planet.

observed 1.746 h vs central_h 1.049 h central ratio 1.664 with fit_b 0.9031 is too long/grazing for the M-dwarf (rad 0.234 Rsun, rp_rearth 1.154); shape v_sigma -4.463 is flat-bottomed but that alone does not outweigh the depth instability.
